summary: Vintage and small consumer electronics: portable audio, CRT monitors, calculators, synthesizers, remotes, under-cabinet appliances, lab surplus and EV charging gear. Built from the sourcing research spreadsheet. The common thread is weight-to-value: most of these are under 1lb with two- to four-figure ceilings, which is the shape that survives the shipping maths. The heavy entries (CRTs, full-size synths, wall chargers) are flagged pickup-or-freight precisely because they do not.
field_workflow: Model number first, always. These markets price by exact model and one digit can mean a 10x difference
Battery bays: leak corrosion is the most common value killer across every category here
Missing accessories (brackets, cases, styluses, power supplies) cut value harder than cosmetic wear does
Non-working is still worth listing for the high tiers; these have active repair communities
Anything over roughly 15lb: assume local pickup, because freight kills the deal
skip_list: Consumer CRT televisions with no RGB or component inputs, freight exceeds value
Modern universal remotes still in production (GE, RCA blister-pack)
Calculators with cracked or delaminating LCDs
Organ and console furniture pieces, bulky and near-unsellable
Level 1 trickle charging cables, shipped free with every EV

era_markers: Model number on the rear label or inside the battery door
Blue/silver TPS-L2 is the 1979 original and the one collectors chase
DD and DC series use quartz-locked capstans, a tier above plastic EX models
Original case, belt clip and headphones lift the price substantially
brands.notes: Belts perish with age, so a unit that spins but chews tape is still worth listing as serviceable. Buyers rebuild these.
condition_critical: Test the play AND fast-forward motors
Check the battery compartment for leak corrosion
Confirm the capstan spins; dried belts are the usual fault

era_markers: PVM and BVM broadcast monitors carry the premium, not consumer KV sets
RGB and component inputs on the rear are the value driver for retro gamers
Screen size sits in the model number (PVM-20L5 is a 20 inch)
brands.notes: Almost always a local-pickup play: a 20 inch PVM is 60lb of glass and freight eats the whole margin. Buy only if you can collect it.
condition_critical: Verify tube brightness; a dim tube is worthless
Check for RGB or component inputs, not just composite
Look for burn-in on the phosphor

era_markers: Red LED display means 1970s Classic series, the collector tier
Serial number sticker in the battery bay dates the unit
An HP-35 without Hewlett-Packard on the bezel is the rare first run
Original leather case, manuals and charger add materially
brands.notes: The best weight-to-value ratio in the whole sheet: under 1lb with a four-figure ceiling on the right model.
condition_critical: Check the LCD for missing segments and bleed
Battery door present; missing doors tank the price
Test every key, membrane failure is common

era_markers: Speak and Spell with physical push buttons (1978-80) beats the later membrane versions
TI-84 Plus CE colour screen is the current school requirement, so demand is steady
Model and revision are on the back label
brands.notes: Graphing calculators sell hardest in August and January. Bought off-season they are worth holding for the school run.
condition_critical: Speak and Spell: test voice synthesis clarity
Check the battery bay for leak damage
Graphing units: verify the screen has no dead columns

era_markers: Serial number engraved on the base
Type II has 11 digits and the larger body
Original metal canister and case are expected at the top of the range

comp_ranges_usd.item: Curta Type I / II with canister

brands.notes: Rare enough that auction lots routinely misidentify it as a pepper grinder or a lens. Worth a second look at anything small, cylindrical and knurled.
condition_critical: Turn the crank; it must move freely without grinding
Verify the canister is the matching original
Check digits advance cleanly across all registers

era_markers: HP-01 (1977) is the four-figure one: gold or steel case, tiny stylus
Casio CA-53W is the common Back to the Future model, modest value
Original bracelet and stylus matter more than case condition
brands.notes: Under 8oz, so shipping is almost free and even the low end clears a useful margin.
condition_critical: Screen clarity; LCD rot kills the value
Test every button, calculator keys are the usual failure
Original band present?

era_markers: Late 80s to late 90s, with a battery bay and IR port on the top edge
Original leather sleeve and manual add a little
brands.notes: Non-working units still sell for parts and for their accessories, and they are close to free in mixed lots.
condition_critical: Does it power on at all?
Screen segments intact?
Battery leak damage in the bay

era_markers: A busy front panel with many sliders and dials signals the analogue era
Roland Jupiter and Juno badging sits on the top left
Serial plate on the rear near the power inlet

comp_ranges_usd.item: Casio CZ and other budget digital

brands.notes: The highest absolute ceiling in the sheet. Even non-working Junos sell well, because the voice chips alone are sought after.
condition_critical: Test every key and every slider
Listen for dead voices; Juno 106 voice chips are a known fault
Confirm the power supply is original, or note that it is missing

era_markers: OEM remotes carry a model number printed on the back
Harmony hubs and charging cradles included lift the price
The Harmony line is discontinued, so no replacements are being made

comp_ranges_usd.item: Common TV and cable OEM remotes

brands.comp_query_template: Universal and OEM remote controls {model} sold
brands.notes: Routinely under a dollar in mixed lots, with an extreme margin. Check the model number on the back before writing any remote off.
condition_critical: Test the IR emitter through a phone camera; it glows on video
Battery bay corrosion is the usual killer
Confirm the exact OEM model number

era_markers: Under-cabinet mounting brackets and template are the value driver
Almond and white 80s and 90s colourways are the sought ones
Model number on the underside plate
brands.notes: The brackets are most of the value: a complete kit is worth roughly three times a bare unit, so check the box for hardware before passing.
condition_critical: Mounting brackets and screws present?
Heating element or motor runs?
Cord and plug undamaged

era_markers: Asset tags from a university or hospital indicate a surplus lot
Model and serial plate on the rear or underside
Calibration stickers with dates suggest it was in service
brands.notes: Government and university surplus is the source. Stick to desktop units, because anything floor-standing is freight and the margin is gone.
condition_critical: Seal integrity on cold storage
Compressor noise on start
Readout clarity, with all segments lit

era_markers: Level 2 units are the valuable ones; Level 1 trickle cables are near worthless
Amperage rating is printed on the unit and drives the price
Tesla adapters are small, high-margin and frequently loose in estate lots
brands.notes: Adapters are under 1lb and carry most of the margin. The wall units are bulky enough that shipping matters, so check the auction ships before bidding.
condition_critical: Verify Level 1 or Level 2 and the amperage
Check the cable for fraying and the plug for burn marks
Factory reset any smart or wifi features before listing

era_markers: Silver-faced receivers from the 1970s are the collected era
McIntosh blue meters and glass front panel are unmistakable
Model number on the rear panel next to the speaker terminals
Wood cases add materially and are often missing
brands.notes: The top of the sheet by resale, and consistently mispriced at estate auctions because a receiver looks like junk furniture. Heavy enough that shipping needs checking before bidding.
condition_critical: Test every channel, both left and right
Listen for crackle when turning the volume pot
No burning or smoke smell; that means a failed output stage
Confirm the wood case is present if the model had one

platform_notes.eBay: Dominant for all of these; buyers search exact model numbers.
platform_notes.Reverb: Better than eBay for synthesizers and anything studio-adjacent.
platform_notes.local_pickup: The only sane route for CRTs and full-size synths.
